Rashi on Arakhin 32b:10:1.hebrew: אלא מקיש ביאתם בימי עזרא כו' - דהא "כי לא עשו" לאו אסוכות מהדר, אלא הכי קאמר: כי לא עשו מה שעשו עכשיו מימות יהושע, ומאי ניהו — קדושת הארץ:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:10:1.english: Rather, it compares their arrival in the days of Ezra, etc. - For [the phrase] "for they had not done [so]" does not refer back to Sukkot; rather, this is what [the verse] is saying: they had not done what they did now since the days of Joshua — and what is that? The sanctification of the Land:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:10:2.english: They counted Sabbatical [years] - [meaning] that they began to count Sabbatical [years] and became obligated in tithes:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:11:1.hebrew: והביאך ה' אלהיך וגו' - בשובם מן הגלות משתעי קרא, דכתיב לעיל מיניה (דברים ל): "ושב ה' אלהיך את שבותך ורחמך":
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:11:1.english: And the Lord your God will bring you, etc. - The verse speaks of their return from the exile, as it is written just before it (Deuteronomy 30): "And the Lord your God will return your captivity and have mercy upon you":

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:12:1.hebrew: ואידך - לעולם "כי לא עשו" אסוכות קאי, ולאו סוכות ממש, אלא דבעא עזרא רחמי איצרא דעבודה זרה ואימסר בידיה, כדאמר בסנהדרין (דף סד.):
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:12:1.english: And the other [tanna] - Actually, [the phrase] "for [they] had not done [so]" refers to sukkot, yet not literal sukkot; rather, Ezra prayed for mercy regarding the [evil] inclination of idol worship, and it was delivered into his hand, as is stated in Sanhedrin (64a):

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:12:2.english: And the merit protected - [the merit] of Ezra [protected] them:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:12:3.hebrew: כי סוכה - כי לא עשו דבר זה בימות יהושע כן, והיינו דקפיד קרא לאדכורי יהושע טפי מהאחרים, וקא מדכר ליה בלשון גנאי:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:12:3.english: Like a sukka - [meaning] that they had not done this thing in the days of Joshua; and this is why the verse was particular to mention Joshua more than the others, and mentions him in a derogatory manner:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:13:1.hebrew: דבכל דוכתא כתיב יהושע והכא ישוע - משום דאיהו הוה ליה למיבעי רחמי עלה דמילתא, דבשלמא משה לא בעא רחמי כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:13:1.english: As in every place it is written Yehoshua, and here Yeshua - [This is] because he should have prayed for mercy regarding this matter, for "granted Moses did not pray for mercy," etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:14:1.english: You possess it - [with] that same sanctification, and there is no need to sanctify [it] again:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:15:1.english: From [the time] that the tribe of Reuben was exiled - in the days of Sennacherib:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:18:1.hebrew: מנו יובלות לקדש שמיטין - ודאי יובל לא היה נוהג, שיהו עבדים נפטרים משום יובל, ולא שדות של מכר חוזרות; אבל שמיטין היו נוהגים, לשמט כספים ולשמט מזרע וקציר. דהא צריכין למנות שנת יובל כדי שיבואו השמיטין במקומן; שלסוף ז' שמיטות היו מניחין שנת נ', שלא היו מונין אותה לשמיטה הבאה, מפני שהיא ראויה להיות שנת יובל, ושנה של אחריה מתחיל המנין. דאם לא היו מונין יובלות, היו מונין אותה שנה לחשבון השמיטין, והוו השמיטין שלא במקומן:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:18:1.english: They counted Jubilee [Years] to sanctify Sabbatical [Years] - Indeed, the Jubilee [law] was not in practice — that slaves would be emancipated on account of the Jubilee, nor that sold fields would return [to their original owners] — however, Sabbatical [Years] were in practice, to remit monetary [debts] and to desist from sowing and reaping. For they needed to count the Jubilee year so that the Sabbatical [Years] would fall in their proper places; for at the end of seven Sabbatical cycles they would leave out the fiftieth year, not counting it toward the next Sabbatical cycle, because it was fit to be a Jubilee year, and [from] the year after it the count would begin. For if they did not count Jubilee [Years], they would count that [fiftieth] year in the reckoning of the Sabbatical [Years], and the Sabbatical [Years] would not be in their proper places:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:1:1.english: Until Gamla - All [the] cities in the Galilee up to Gamla were surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:2:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - האי תנא אתא לפרושי מתני', והכי קאמר: גמלא דקתני מתני' דהוות מוקפת חומה מימות יהושע, היינו גמלא דגליל:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:2:1.english: Rava said - This tanna [of the baraita] comes to explain the Mishnah, and this is what he is saying: The Gamla that the Mishnah teaches was surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua is the Gamla of the Galilee:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:2:2.hebrew: לאפוקי - דאי איכא גמלא בעבר הירדן וביהודה, לא הויא מוקפת חומה מימות יהושע, וכן גדוד; וכן חדיד וירושלים ביהודה, לאפוקי עיירות שבגליל ועבר הירדן שנקראו חדיד ואונו וירושלים — אינן מוקפות מימות יהושע:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:2:2.english: To the exclusion of - That if there is a Gamla in Transjordan or in Judea, it was not surrounded by a wall since the days of Joshua, and similarly [regarding] Gedod; and similarly, Hadid and Jerusalem in Judea [are specified] to the exclusion of cities in the Galilee and Transjordan that were called Hadid, Ono, and Jerusalem — [for] they are not walled since the days of Joshua:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:2:3.hebrew: אינך דליכא כותייהו - אינך דקא חשיב במתני', כגון קצרה ויודפת, דליכא בדוכתא אחריתי דמסקי כשמתייהו, לא איצטריך למיתני ברייתא בהי ארעא קיימי:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:2:3.english: Those others, where there are none like them - Those other [cities] that [the Tanna] enumerates in the Mishnah, such as Katzrah and Yodfat — since there are none in any other place that are called by their names — it was not necessary for the baraita to teach in which land they are located:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:3:1.hebrew: עשרה דברים - מפרש בב"ק בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא דף פב:), וזה אחד מהם:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:3:1.english: Ten matters - [These are] explained in Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 82b), and this is one of them:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:3:2.hebrew: אין הבית חלוט - משום דכתיב (ויקרא כה): "לקונה אותו לדורותיו", וקסבר לא נתחלקה ירושלים לשבטים, ומאן קא מקני ליה:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:3:2.english: A house is not transferred in perpetuity - Because it is written (Leviticus 25): "to the one who buys it for his generations," and he holds [that] Jerusalem was not divided among the tribes, so who transfers ownership [of it] to him?

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:4:1.hebrew: לאו מי אמר רב יוסף וכו' - במס' מכות, בפ' אלו הן הגולין (מכות דף י.):
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:4:1.english: Didn't Rav Yosef say, etc. - In Tractate Makkot, in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Hen HaGolin (Makkot 10a):

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:5:1.english: These - [the cities] listed in our Mishnah:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:5:2.hebrew: וקידשום - מפרש במסכת שבועות (דף טז.) דמקדשי לה בשתי תודות ובשיר, ובית דין מהלכין ושתי תודות אחריהן וכו':
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:5:2.english: And they sanctified them - [The Gemara] explains in Tractate Shevuot (16a) that they sanctify it with two thanksgiving-offerings and with song, and the court walks with two thanksgiving-offerings [carried] behind them, etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:5:3.hebrew: בטלו - שאין קדושת הארץ נוהגת בהן, ואין בהן דין ערי חומה:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:5:3.english: Were nullified - for the sanctity of the Land [of Israel] does not apply to them, and they do not have the law of walled cities:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:5:4.english: When the sanctity of the land was nullified - at the first destruction [of the Temple]:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:5:5.english: Initial consecration - that Joshua consecrated it:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:6:1.hebrew: הא אמרת - לקמן בסוף דהא מילתא, דלא צריכי לקדושי, דקתני סיפא: "ולא אלו בלבד אלא כל שתעלה בידך כו'", שקידשה לשעתה ולעתיד לבא:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:6:1.english: Have you not said - later, at the end of this statement, that they do not need to be sanctified, as the latter clause [of the baraita] teaches: "And not these alone, but any [city] that comes into your hand, etc.," because [its original sanctification] sanctified it [both] for its own time and for the future to come:

Rashi on Arakhin 32b:8:1.hebrew: חדא מינייהו - הך דקתני קידשה לעתיד לבא, ר' אלעזר בר יוסי אמרה, כי היכי דקאמר "אע"פ שאין לו עכשיו", ואע"ג דחרוב, לא בטלה קדושתיה:
Rashi on Arakhin 32b:8:1.english: One of them - That [baraita] which teaches [that the first sanctification] sanctified it for all future time, Rabbi Elazar bar Yosei stated it — just as he says, "even if it does not have [a wall] now," [meaning that] even though it was destroyed, its sanctity was not nullified:

Tosafot on Arakhin 32b:10:1.hebrew: וקדשו ערי חומה - פי': לענין מכירת בית בבתי ערי חומה, ולענין שילוח מצורעים חוץ לעיר; דדוקא בבתי ערי חומה צריך לשלוח המצורעים חוץ לחומה, אבל שאר (ארצות) [עיירות] לא. ואבנים מנוגעות צריך לשלוח חוץ לעיר, ואפי' לא היו מוקפות מימות יהושע. והכי תניא בתורת כהנים: "אתהן חוץ לעיר" — ואין אדם חוץ לכל העיר, אלא חוץ לעיירות המוקפות חומה בלבד. וא"ת: מנלן? הא לא כתיב "בית חומה" גבי אדם מצורע! ואומר הרב רבינו יצחק, דגמרינן "חוץ למחנה מושבו" דכתיב ביה במצורע (ויקרא י״ג:מ״ו) מ"מושב" דכתיב "בית מושב עיר חומה" (שם כה). ופירש רש"י כאן, דמקדש ליה (לארעא) בשתי תודות ובשיר, ובית דין מהלכין ושתי תודות אחריהן, כדאיתא בשבועות (דף טז. ושם). ובמס' שבועות פירש"י, דאשכחן שהיו מקדשין חומות ירושלים בשתי תודות ובשיר כשבאו להוסיף על העיר ועל (העיירות) [העזרות]; אבל שאר (ארצות) [עיירות] לא ידעתי היאך היו מקדשין אותן:
Tosafot on Arakhin 32b:10:1.english: And they sanctified walled cities - Meaning: with respect to the sale of a house in [the law of] houses of walled cities, and with respect to sending lepers outside the city; for specifically in [the case of] houses of walled cities must one send lepers outside the wall, whereas [in] other towns [one does] not. And [regarding] afflicted stones, one must send [them] outside the city even if they were not walled from the days of Joshua. And so it was taught in Torat Kohanim: "[You shall cast] them outside the city" — [that applies to stones,] and not [to] a person [being sent] outside every city, rather outside cities surrounded by a wall only. And if you will ask: From where do we [know this]? Behold, "walled house" is not written regarding a leprous person! And the Rav, Rabbeinu Yitzchak, says that we derive [it from] "outside the camp shall his dwelling [moshavo] be," which is written regarding a leper (Leviticus 13:46), from "dwelling [moshav]," which is written [in] "a dwelling house of a walled city" (ibid. 25[:29]). And Rashi explained here that one sanctifies it with two thanksgiving-offerings and with song, and the court walks with two thanksgiving-offerings behind them, as is stated in Shevuot (16a and there). And in tractate Shevuot, Rashi explained that we find that they would sanctify the walls of Jerusalem with two thanksgiving-offerings and with song when they came to add to the city and to the Temple courtyards; but [as for] other towns, I do not know how they would sanctify them:

Tosafot on Arakhin 32b:18:1.hebrew: מנו יובלות לקדש שמיטין - מכאן תימה לברייתא דתני בירושלמי דמסכת גיטין, ורש"י כתב בפ' השולח (גיטין דף לו.) דתניא בירושלמי: "וזה דבר השמיטה שמוט" — בשתי שמיטות הכתוב מדבר, אחד שמיטת יובל ואחד שמיטת שביעית; בזמן שאתה משמט [יובל] אתה משמט [שביעית], בזמן שאי אתה משמט יובל אי אתה משמט שביעית. וכאן אומר דלא מנו יובלות אלא לקדש שמיטין! ופירש רש"י פ' השולח (שם) דההיא דערכין דמדרבנן היא. ואין משמע כן בת"כ (ואומר אני דתנאי היא (עכ"ל רש"י) (דהא דירושלמי רבי היא) ועוד אור"ת דהך ברייתא דמייתי) ריש פרק השולח (שם): "וזה דבר השמיטה שמוט" — בשתי שמיטות הכתוב מדבר, אחת שמיטת קרקע ואחת שמיטת כספים; והא דירושלמי רבי היא. אבל רבנן פליגי עליה דרבי ואמרי: מנין דיש שמיטה אף על פי שאין יובל? ת"ל (ויקרא כ״ה:ח׳) "והיו לך שבע שבתות השנים"; ומנין שיעשה יובל אע"פ שאין שביעית? ת"ל (שם) "והיו לך תשע וארבעים שנה". [וסוגיא] דהכא אתיא כרבנן. מיהו יש ליישב ההיא דתורת כהנים אפי' כר': והא דתני "שביעית אע"פ שאין יובל", יש לפרשה אע"פ שלא נהגו יובל והניחו בחטאם, וכדתני בפ"ק דראש השנה (דף ט: ושם): "יובל היא" — אע"פ שלא שמטו ואע"פ שלא תקעו; יכול אע"פ שלא שלחו? ת"ל "היא", דברי ר' יהודה. רבי יוסי אומר: יובל אע"פ שלא שמטו ואע"פ שלא שלחו; יכול אף על פי שלא תקעו? ת"ל "היא":
Tosafot on Arakhin 32b:18:1.english: They counted Jubilees in order to sanctify Sabbatical years - From here there is a difficulty regarding the baraita that is taught in the Jerusalem Talmud of Tractate Gittin, and Rashi wrote in the chapter [entitled] HaShole'aḥ (Gittin 36a) that it is taught in the Jerusalem Talmud: "And this is the matter of the release: release" — Scripture speaks of two releases, one the release of the Jubilee and one the release of the Sabbatical year; when you release [in the Jubilee], you release [in the Sabbatical year], [and] when you do not release [in the] Jubilee, you do not release [in the] Sabbatical year. Yet here it says that they only counted Jubilees in order to sanctify Sabbatical years! And Rashi explained [in] the chapter [entitled] HaShole'aḥ (ibid.) that that [passage] in Arakhin is by rabbinic decree. But it does not imply thus in Torat Kohanim (and I say that it is [a dispute of] Tannaim (thus far the words of Rashi) (for that [baraita] of the Jerusalem Talmud is [the view of] Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi]). Furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam says that this baraita that is cited) [at] the beginning of the chapter [entitled] HaShole'aḥ (ibid.): "And this is the matter of the release: release" — Scripture speaks of two releases, one the release of land and one the release of debts; and that [baraita] of the Jerusalem Talmud is [the view of] Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi]. However, the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] and say: From where [do we derive] that there is a Sabbatical year even though there is no Jubilee? The verse states (Leviticus 25:8): "And you shall have seven weeks of years"; and from where [do we derive] that a Jubilee is observed even though there is no Sabbatical year? The verse states (ibid.): "And you shall have forty-nine years." And the sugya here follows the Rabbis. However, one can reconcile that [teaching] of Torat Kohanim even according to Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi]: that which it teaches, "a Sabbatical year even though there is no Jubilee," one can explain it [as meaning] even though they did not observe the Jubilee and abandoned [it] through their sin, just as it is taught in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (9b and there): "It is a Jubilee" — even though they did not release [land] and even though they did not blow [the shofar]; one might think even though they did not emancipate [slaves]? The verse states "it is" — [these are] the words of Rabbi Yehudah. Rabbi Yosei says: [It is] a Jubilee even though they did not release and even though they did not emancipate; one might think even though they did not blow [the shofar]? The verse states "it is":

Tosafot on Arakhin 32b:4:1.hebrew: הכא נמי תרתי ירושלים הוו - ותימה, דלרבא נמי אנו צריכין לומר כן, דתרי ירושלים הוו! וי"ל: דלרבא אין אנו צריכין לומר ביהודה תרי ירושלים הוו, אלא בשאר ארצות; אבל לרב אשי, צ"ל ביהודה תרי ירושלים הוו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 32b:4:1.english: Here too, there were two [places called] Jerusalem - And it is astonishing, for according to Rava too we must say so, that there were two [places called] Jerusalem! And one can say: according to Rava, we do not need to say [that] in Judea there were two [places called] Jerusalem, but rather [one in Judea and one] in other lands; but according to Rav Ashi, one must say [that] in Judea [itself] there were two [places called] Jerusalem:
